platforms.name: Printify
platforms.blurb: Print-on-demand: shops, blueprints, products, orders, publishing.
platforms.note: Create a personal access token under Printify → Settings → API.
platforms.apiNotes: Mockups are read-only and have no endpoint of their own: they are the images[] (src, variant_ids, position, is_default) of GET /v1/shops/{shop_id}/products/{product_id}.json. Upload artwork with POST /v1/uploads/images.json and {"file_name":"art.png","url":"https://..."} or {"file_name":"art.png","contents":"${file:path/art.png}"}; read it back with GET /v1/uploads/{image_id}.json. Update with PUT /v1/shops/{shop_id}/products/{product_id}.json: a partial document is accepted, but if you send variants, EVERY variant of the product must be in the request. A product is locked while publishing (is_locked); POST .../products/{product_id}/publishing_succeeded.json or publishing_failed.json unlocks it. Variant catalog: GET /v1/catalog/blueprints/{blueprint_id}/print_providers/{print_provider_id}/variants.json (?show-out-of-stock=1 includes out-of-stock). Ids are opaque strings (e.g. 5de6593ebff03b5313567d22): copy them exactly from a response, never retype or shorten them. Limits: 600 requests/min, catalog 100/min, publishing 200 per 30 min. Product documents are large: pass web_request select, e.g. ["id","variants[].id","variants[].is_enabled","variants[].price","print_areas","images[].src"].
